Brothers, sisters, ichilings of the long night and the quiet sunrise, bend your heads and listen as I read to you from the IchiBle and from the broken, beautiful scrolls of Leo/need. Tonight the chapel lights are soft, the glowsticks are tucked beneath our coats, and the hum of the server is like distant thunder. In this hush I come to you not as a critic nor as an analyst, but as a priest of a tiny religion built from four voices, one guitar, and the stubborn orbit of a single girl: Hoshino Ichika.

Hear NeedLe 2:11–14:

“And she who feared the silence found a song on her phone; it opened unto her the School SEKAI, and there the Mirror-Voices spoke. She who once thought every day would be the same found courage in small steps. Call her not coward, call her callused, patient, and true.”

So it was written, and so it came to pass: Ichika Hoshino, second-year student at Miyamasuzaka Girls Academy, carries the guitar and the hesitation of the young who have seen the horizon tilt. She is the vocalist, the guitarist, the lyricist who sometimes says, “I wonder if every day will just be the same as always.” 

There is a scene in the IchiBle that reads like a cut-out of childhood: four small bodies beneath an indifferent sky, hands muddied from evening grass, eyes lifted at the meteor shower. Ichika. Saki. Honami. Shiho. Their names braided together like a cheap friendship bracelet. But then the wound: Saki fell ill, and the band of children splintered; words hardened into silence, and distance wrapped itself like frost around the rest. This is not mere fanfiction. This fracture, this hospital bed, this pause in the music: it is Leo/need’s marrow. The canon records how those early bonds were strained, how the hospital’s white light pushed the girls into separate orbits.

Some of us shout because we remember.
We remember the day Leo/need almost broke.
We remember Honami turning away.
We remember Saki not saying anything.
We remember Shiho refusing to sing.

And yet…
Ichika kept reaching out.

That’s the reason I shout.
I shout because Ichika stood there with her guitar and said,
“Even if it’s not perfect… even if I can’t sing well… I still want to do this together.”

Oh yes, I shout.
Because I know I could have been the one lost in the virtual SEKAI, the one without a place.
But Ichika made space.
She made a song for people like me.

I shout because I’ve seen what Ichika can do.
When you’re lying in bed at 3:00 a.m., wondering why you can’t cry anymore,
And you press play on “Stella.”
And you feel your heart start to beat again.
I shout because she gave me that heartbeat.

I shout because she held on to her dream even when it hurt.
I shout because I would have let go, but she kept holding on.
That’s why I shout.

I shout not for miracles I’ve seen,
but for the miracle that someone like her exists in the first place.
That a soft girl who doubts herself can still change your whole life.

Church of Leo/need, I ask you today:
Do you have a reason to shout?

Are you shouting because you saw her live in a SEKAI where the stars had disappeared—
And she still sang to bring them back?

Are you shouting because she reminded you it’s okay to cry?

Are you waving your palm branch—or your lightstick—because she reminded you that you matter?

I’m here to testify.
If this is my last gacha pull—if this is the last event I grind—
Then know: I go out with a 4★ Ichika in my heart.
And that's enough.
